title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context from pp. 26-28. For smooth projective X, Grothendieck introduces a relation on cycles finer than algebraic equivalence; Remark 1.5 on p.28 calls it 'équiv. d'Alb.' Take a smooth projective connected parameter variety T (the margin of p.28 stresses T projective), a cycle Z on X×T, and a 0-cycle V on T of degree 0 whose Albanese sum S_T(V) is zero in Alb(T). A cycle is Albanese-equivalent to 0 if it is (a sum of cycles) of the form Z(V) = pr_{X*}(Z·(X×V)).

In modern terms the subgroup is the sum over all correspondences Γ: T → X of Γ_*(T(T)), where T(T) = ker(alb: CH_0(T)_{deg 0} → Alb(T)). It contains the rationally trivial cycles: take T = P^1, where every degree-0 0-cycle has S = 0. The quotient is written A'^*(X).

The previous page proves property (ii), compatibility with pullback f^*. Represent z = Z(V), move (Z,V) inside their linear-equivalence classes to (Z',V') so that (f×id_T)^*Z' and Z'(V') are defined. Then intersection theory gives f^*(Z'(V')) = Z'_1(V').

This page:
(1) The moving-lemma verification for the existence of Z',V' is left 'à rédiger'.
(2) Property (iii), intersection products, is proved like (ii). Reduce to z, z' built from the same T, V and two cycles Z, Z'. Alternatively, reduce to exterior (cartesian) products plus pullback along the diagonal, which avoids moving cycles. The underlying identity is Z(V)·z' = (Z·(z'×T))(V).
(3) Property (iv) is proved 'par l'AQT' (abbreviation unclear).
(4) Property (v) is trivial from the definitions, like the functoriality of algebraic equivalence.
(5) Scholie 1.3: the A'^*(X) have the same general functorial properties as Chow groups A^*(X), including the projection formula. So Albanese equivalence is an adequate equivalence relation in Samuel's sense, lying between rational and algebraic equivalence.
(6) Whenever linear and algebraic equivalence coincide on X (a point, P^n, flag varieties), Albanese equivalence also coincides with them. It is sandwiched between the two, so this is immediate.

The page serves the program of the dossier: classifying adequate equivalence relations for the standard/Hodge/Tate conjectures. Theorem 1.4 on the next page then identifies the relation on 0-cycles (degree 0 and Albanese sum 0) and on divisors (= linear equivalence).
errors: The key moving-lemma step (existence of Z', V' with the required intersections defined) is explicitly left unproved ('Nous laissons ici le détail'). It is standard via Chow's moving lemma on smooth projective varieties, so this is a gap in writing, not mathematics.
No mathematical error visible. The final claim (lin = alg on X implies Alb-equivalence = lin) is correct because rational ⊂ Albanese ⊂ algebraic equivalence.

Related (next page, Remark 1.5): the open question whether Albanese equivalence equals linear equivalence, already for 0-cycles, was answered negatively by Mumford (1968/69) for surfaces with p_g > 0. If this page predates that, Grothendieck's hesitation is consistent with the state of knowledge.

ideas.what: Equivalence relation on cycles generated by images under correspondences of Albanese-kernel 0-cycles on smooth projective parameter varieties ('équivalence d'Albanese').
ideas.modern_name: Second step F^2 of the Saito filtration on Chow groups; Albanese-kernel/Bloch–Beilinson-type filtration (closely related)
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Saito (c. 1979-80, generalized Albanese and filtrations on Chow groups); later Bloch, Beilinson, Murre, Jannsen
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as far as known; possibly circulated in Grothendieck's 1960s discussions on standard conjectures

ideas.what: Scholie 1.3: Albanese equivalence is stable under pullback, pushforward and intersection product, with the projection formula; i.e. it is an adequate equivalence relation.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Samuel (1958) for the notion; adequacy of the Saito filtration steps is standard later

ideas.what: Reducing intersection products to exterior products plus diagonal pullback to avoid moving cycles.
ideas.modern_name: Standard reduction to the diagonal (Fulton–MacPherson style)

ideas.what: On varieties where linear and algebraic equivalence agree (P^n, flag varieties), all intermediate adequate relations agree.

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines (pp. 26-28) Albanese equivalence, the cycles Σ Γ_*(ker alb_T), and asserts in Scholie 1.3 that it is an adequate relation with full functoriality. This anticipates the F^2 step of the Saito filtration (c. 1979) by over a decade, if the page dates from c. 1965.
missed.quote: Scholie 1.3. Les A'^*(X), pour X variable, ont les mêmes propriétés fonctorielles générales que les A^*(X). En particulier, ... la formule de projection
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: Grothendieck had the correspondence-generated Albanese-kernel relation as an adequate relation, a precursor of Bloch–Beilinson filtrations. Together with Remark 1.5 (next page), he explicitly posed whether it equals rational equivalence, the question Mumford answered for surfaces with p_g > 0 and which Bloch's conjecture addresses for p_g = 0.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a routine proof sketch of adequacy. The interest lies in the relation being treated, an Albanese equivalence defined via correspondences, which is essentially F^2 of the later Saito filtration and appears here possibly c. 1965. This is a modest priority point rather than a hidden theorem.
transcription_corrections: 'On prouve (iii) par [la même] méthode que (ii)': the first numeral is (iii), the second (ii). The struck-out word before 'méthode' is crossed out and 'la même' is likely.

'en se ramenant au cas où 𝔷, 𝔷′ sont définis en termes des [mêmes] T, 𝔙 et deux cycles Z, Z′ sur [Y×]T': the letters are cycle symbols (𝔷/z), not 𝔙, and the second symbol is the 0-cycle 𝔙 rather than U.
'Celle de (v) est triviale sur les définitions (comme sur la fonctorialité de l'équiv. alg.)': close to the image.

Last lines: 'Dans les cas où équiv. linéaire = équiv. alg. sur X (p.ex. lorsque X ponctuel, les P^n, les variétés de drapeaux) ils sont = équiv. alb[?]'. Probably meaning the A' coincide with the A, i.e. Albanese equivalence = linear equivalence there.
First-line marginal note reads 'à rédiger' (underlined), consistent with the transcription.
